title: POC SLO contract, workload sizing and benchmark timetable
meeting_header: Date: 2026-03-12; Start: 16:00 PST; Duration: 52m; Recording: yes; Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Oliver Nguyen (Bluecrest CTO), Priya Rao (Bluecrest ML Eng), Samir Das (Bluecrest SRE), Allison Kim (Bluecrest PM)
summary: Align on POC success criteria and finalize an SLO 'contract' for TTFT vs TPOT, define p95/p99 targets, agree workload sizing and benchmark timetable. Decide sampling plan (synthetic vs production replay), capacity knobs (batching, quantization), and a 4-week pilot timeline with bench windows and acceptance gates.
topics: Define TTFT and TPOT acceptance thresholds (p95/p99)
Traffic profile and payload size distribution
Benchmark methodology: cold vs warm cache; synthetic vs replay
action_items: Maya Patel; Send pilot pricing + two capacity options (dedicated burst vs shared hosted) ; due 2026-03-19
Ethan Cole; Draft benchmark script + JMeter/vegeta configs and share bucket for results; due 2026-03-16
Priya Rao; Provide 7 days of anonymized request traces and payload-size histogram; due 2026-03-17
Samir Das; Confirm network egress constraints and KMS requirements for Private option; due 2026-03-18
All; 4-week pilot start date target: 2026-03-30; confirm by 2026-03-20
next_steps: Redwood to submit two pilot proposals (hosted cost-optimized + dedicated predictable) by 3/19
Customer to upload traces to shared S3 staging by 3/17
Schedule benchmark run window week of 3/23 (3 runs: cold, warm, steady-state)
Follow-up working session to review initial bench results: 3/25
transcript: [00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — we'll keep this focused on SLOs and the bench timetable. Oliver, Priya, can you remind us of the key success criteria from your side?

[00:22] Oliver Nguyen: Sure. For Bluecrest we need two things; first latency experience in the app — low perceived delay on first assistant response — and second cost predictability. We also have compliance questions but we'll park those for the security call.

[00:40] Priya Rao: Yep, specifically for chat we want to measure first token latency but also per-token throughput for bulk inference. Our product team has asked for p95 and p99 numbers for both metrics.

[01:05] Ethan Cole: Great. Just to align on definitions: TTFT is time-to-first-token measured from request accept to first token emitted. TPOT is total per-token average compute time (we usually report per-token median and p95/p99 in ms). Is that how you think about it?
[01:28] Priya Rao: Yes. And for business we care about TTFT p95 under 300ms ideally, p99 under 700ms. For TPOT we want p95 under 25ms, p99 under 80ms — ballpark, happy to adjust after benching.

[01:50] Maya Patel: Those are reasonable starting targets. For the POC we should codify an acceptance 'contract' — i.e., if 3 out of 4 bench windows meet the p95/p99 targets on your production profile, we pass. Thoughts?

[02:12] Samir Das: Sounds ok but we need to be explicit about warm vs cold cache — our real SLOs should be based on warm cache numbers because we use prefix caching heavily. Cold starts happen but are rare. We'll want separate windows for cold-start tolerance.

[02:36] Lena Ortiz: Agreed. Our suggested measurement plan: run three sweeps per bench day: cold-cache (service restart, 1 run), warm-cache ramp (after 15 min steady traffic), and steady-state sampling. Each sweep should be at least 1k requests sampled across sizes.
[02:58] Oliver Nguyen: FYI our request length distribution: 60% short prompts (~20 tokens), 30% medium (~80 tokens), 10% long (>250 tokens). We can provide histograms. That will affect TPOT heavily.
[03:18] Ethan Cole: Valuable — we'll use a weighted mix in the synthetic driver or replay your traces. For throughput sizing: what QPS do you expect at peak?
[03:30] Allison Kim: Peak is about 120 QPS now for the assistant feature, but we have burst windows up to 220 QPS around morning syncs. Concurrency matters a lot for batching behavior.

[03:48] Maya Patel: Ok so for pilot bench plan we'll sweep at 25 QPS, 120 QPS and 220 QPS with your traffic mix. We'll run on our recommended model variant (quantized-4) and, as a fallback, unquantized baseline to show delta. Any objections?
[04:06] Priya Rao: No objections. Also curious about GPU assumptions — what instance types will you use in the dedicated proposal?

[04:15] Ethan Cole: For dedicated sizing we propose H100 or A100 80GB equivalents depending on budget. For quantized-4 we typically show near-H100 throughput on cheaper A100 for many LLMs, but we'll show both. We'll include a note about KV-cache warmup which reduces TTFT in practice.
[04:40] Oliver Nguyen: Can you clarify how you measure TTFT across the whole stack? We have network egress variability across regions, could that skew results?

[04:54] Lena Ortiz: We'll instrument at the Redwood edge and measure request accept -> first token emit. We'll provide both edge-to-edge and server-only numbers. For network concerns we'll also run a replay from a VM inside your VPC (if Private) to isolate infra noise.
[05:15] Samir Das: For private we'd need to validate KMS key wrap and audit logs; that'll be a separate security pass but it impacts timeline if we require on-prem hardware commissioning.

[05:30] Maya Patel: Noted. For acceptance gates in the SLO contract, propose: requirement A) TTFT p95 <= 300ms and p99 <= 700ms for warm-cache steady-state at 120 QPS; B) TPOT p95 <= 30ms and p99 <= 90ms across weighted payload mix; C) throughput headroom to handle 220 QPS bursts with graceful degradation. If 2 of 3 hold we consider conditional pass with remediations. Does that map?
[06:05] Oliver Nguyen: That mapping is fine. We need exact numbers in writing though — 'conditional pass' triggers a 2-week extension to tune batching and caching, right?
[06:18] Maya Patel: Yes, we propose a two-week tune window for failed gates, with specific runbooks. We'll include that in the pilot SLA doc.
[06:30] Priya Rao: On sampling size — you mentioned 1k per sweep earlier. Statistically for p99 I prefer larger samples, like 5k, to get stable tails. Can you support that?

[06:45] Ethan Cole: We can increase to 5k for steady-state p99 accuracy. For cold-start it's harder but we can do 1k restarts across time buckets. Bench run durations will expand accordingly but still doable in 3-4 hour windows.
[07:05] Allison Kim: Timeline constraints: we'd like results before end of March for a Q2 launch decision. So can you commit to bench week of 3/23 and follow-up 3/25?
[07:20] Maya Patel: Yes, bench week of 3/23 with working session 3/25 to review. Pilot start target 3/30. We'll send the formal timetable and runbook.
[07:35] Oliver Nguyen: Also include error budget burn guidance. If p99 breaches by more than 2x during bench we'll consider it a blocker, not just a tune item.

[07:50] Lena Ortiz: We'll include a risk matrix: categorizing breaches (latency tail, correctness regressions, throughput collapse) and proposed mitigations (reduce batch size, enable model fallback, route to smaller context model).
[08:08] Priya Rao: For measurement, can we get token-level breakdowns? We want per-token timing distribution to see where long tokens sit (e.g., kv cache misses).
[08:20] Ethan Cole: Absolutely — our bench artifacts include per-token histograms, sequence length vs latency heatmaps, and traces for failed requests.
[08:35] Samir Das: On reproducibility — we require the bench scripts and drivers so we can re-run internally. Will you open-source the harness or share it?

[08:46] Maya Patel: We'll share the harness and a runbook under a shared repo (read-only for now). We'll also provide a Dockerized runner for replaying traces into the Redwood edge or your private endpoint.
[09:01] Allison Kim: Pricing question — is there a different metric for hosted vs dedicated in pilot? We prefer predictable monthly committed throughput for early stages.

[09:12] Maya Patel: We'll provide two proposals: 1) hosted with usage billing + burst cap; 2) dedicated with monthly commit and headroom. We'll include per-token and per-hour GPU baseline numbers so you can compare.
[09:30] Oliver Nguyen: Competitor fit — we evaluated Anthropic and they had higher per-token latency but better cost at scale; curious how Redwood compares on token efficiency.
[09:42] Ethan Cole: We'll include a comparative row (public benchmarked numbers) but won't claim parity; objective is to show your traffic on our stack and produce side-by-side runs.
[09:55] Priya Rao: Ok, quick note on observability: we need token-level billing and per-route dashboards; will that be available in the console during pilot?
[10:08] Lena Ortiz: Yes, Redwood Console will show per-route latency, token breakdown, per-token cost, and traces. We'll provision views for your team and share dashboard links.

[10:22] Maya Patel: Let's capture explicit bench schedule: Week of 3/23 — Day 1: synthetic sweeps (cold/warm/steady), Day 2: replay using your traces, Day 3: stress burst tests and fallback validation. Report on 3/25 morning. Does that work?
[10:40] Allison Kim: Works for us.
[10:45] Oliver Nguyen: A couple more technical clarifications: will you test with model variants pinned? We want to see quantized-4 and a baseline FP16 run.
[10:55] Ethan Cole: Yes, we'll produce both variants' outputs; note that heavy quantization can impact output quality slightly — we recommend a small eval prompt set to confirm quality post-quant.
[11:08] Priya Rao: We'll prepare a 50-prompt eval set for quality checks; can you run that as part of the bench?
[11:18] Maya Patel: Yes — we'll include an eval step pre/post quantization and include rouge/bleu-style and human-likert snapshot metrics.
[11:32] Samir Das: Last question on SLO pass criteria: is there a requirement on error rate? We need <0.1% 500-level errors in steady-state.
[11:43] Lena Ortiz: We'll add error-rate threshold to the contract: steady-state 5xx < 0.1% and timeouts < 0.2% over bench windows.

[11:55] Maya Patel: Great. To recap — action items: Maya to send proposals; Ethan to share bench harness; Priya/Samir to upload traces and infra constraints. We book the bench window 3/23 and review 3/25. Any final comments?
[12:10] Oliver Nguyen: Nothing else. Thanks everyone. We'll get traces uploaded.
[12:18] Maya Patel: Thanks — we'll follow up with calendar invites and the pilot SLA draft. Meeting adjourned.
[52:00] <recording end>
